root.name: Sicilian Defense: Prins Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. f3

overview: White plays 5.f3 to support e4 and prepare Be3, Qd2 and a kingside pawn storm or a Maroczy-style clamp, delaying Nc3. Black can answer 5...e5 with a Najdorf-like structure after Nb3, or 5...a6 and ...e6 with a Scheveningen feel. Positions often resemble the English Attack, with opposite-side castling and mutual attacks, but 5...e5 6.Nb3 steers toward a slower game.

white_ideas.idea: Build the English Attack set-up: Be3, Qd2, Nc3, O-O-O and a g4 pawn storm.
Meet ...e5 with Nb3 and play c4 or Nc3 for a space edge.

black_ideas.idea: Strike with ...e5 to claim the centre and the d5 square, or ...a6 and ...e6 for Scheveningen play.
Counterattack on the queenside with ...b5 and ...Nbd7 after White commits to opposite-side castling.

typical_structures.structure: Black d6/e5 chain (Najdorf-like) against White e4/f3 with a knight on b3.
Scheveningen small centre d6/e6 with White's f3/e4 pawns.

character.notes: 5.f3 invites English Attack-style opposite-side attacks and an unbalanced race; the 5...e5 6.Nb3 branch is slower.

structure.notes: Open Sicilian with an asymmetrical centre and the half-open c-file.

approach.notes: Standard anti-Najdorf move order, occasionally chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are clear but the attack versus counterattack race needs judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...e5 6.Nb3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. f3 e5 6. Nb3
sublines_that_differ.how: A slower, positional game around the d5 hole, less sharp than the English Attack branches.

character.reason: Open Sicilian with f3 usually leads to opposite-side attacks, though 5...e5 is quieter.

soundness.reason: A respected variation for both sides.

structure.reason: Asymmetrical Sicilian centre with a half-open c-file.

level.reason: Plans clearer than the Najdorf, less theory.

plans.reason: English Attack-style race and the d5 hole after ...e5.
